question: Does indexing RCW 59.18.230's ten enumerated prohibitions separately make the section retrievable, and what does it cost?
verdict: retrieval fixed, product regressed on 2026-07-29 and NOT shipped; re-gated 2026-08-05 with the blocker gone — see revisited_2026_08_05

gold_scan_shipped_published.note: already measured and published; not re-run, per the no-reruns-for-prettier-numbers rule

the_false_red.clause: 2. RENT. Rent is $2,450 per month, due on the first. Payments may be made by check, money order, or electronic transfer through the resident portal.
the_false_red.retrieved: RCW 59.18.230(2)(j) — 'Agrees to make rent payments through electronic means only'
the_false_red.why_it_is_false: The clause PERMITS three payment methods, two of them non-electronic. It is the opposite of an electronic-only mandate. Reproduced twice: green under the shipped index (where (2)(j) never arrives), red under the split.
the_false_red.mechanism: Making the governing prohibition reachable put a crisp, narrow rule in front of the judge, which then over-applied it to a permissive clause on the same topic. A retrieval fix surfaced a generation weakness that the missing document had been masking.

conclusion: The split is the only one of three candidates that moved the strict retrieval metric: hybrid .656, section completion .492 (unchanged), enumerated split .984.
It bought nothing on the gold set's outcome metrics, which were already perfect: 18/18 red and 18/18 citations under the shipped index.
It cost the cleanest published claim in the project — 0 false reds became 1, precision 1.000 -> .947.
So the strict metric is a LEADING INDICATOR, not an outcome. It correctly found a real retrieval gap; closing that gap made the product worse. Outcome metrics win.
Kept implemented and measured, enabled nowhere, same disposition as hybrid retrieval and section completion.

revisited_2026_08_05.why: The roadmap said shipping this needed a labelled permissive-vs-mandatory set rather than a prompt rule written against the single observed false red. That set now exists (evaluation/permissive_pairs.jsonl, 32 clauses across all ten prohibitions) and it said the opposite of what was expected, so the paid gold gate was re-run.
revisited_2026_08_05.what_changed_underneath: Nothing in the clause judge: `judge_clause` and `make_judge_prompt` are unchanged since bb0243e apart from a ScanMeter->UsageMeter annotation, and retrieval.py's diff is metering plumbing. What did change is the index — `build_enumerated_collection.py` gained `temperature=0` after this experiment (commit 210a9e0), the collection was rebuilt, and the RETRIEVAL metric was re-verified at .984 while the PAID PRECISION GATE was not re-run. So the published 'precision 1.000 -> .947' described an index that no longer exists. Provider-side drift on gpt-4.1-mini is the other candidate and cannot be excluded from outside; either way the gate result below is the current one.

permissive_labelled_set.reading: The split is better on both axes, not merely not-worse: it flags 10/10 prohibited clauses where the shipped index flags 8/10 (it reads the exculpation and arbitration-cost prohibitions as green with no citation at all), and it produces 0 false reds where the shipped index produces 2, both on (2)(h) and both citing RCW 59.18.340 instead.

the_false_red_did_not_reproduce.2026_07_29: red under the split, reproduced twice
the_false_red_did_not_reproduce.2026_08_05: not red under the split, in two labelled-set runs and the gold gate

conclusion: The gold gate passes under the split: 18/18 red, 18/18 citations, 0 false reds, 6/6 protections — identical outcomes to the shipped index, plus strict scan retrieval .492 -> .984.

So the stated blocker is gone and the disposition is a decision rather than a constraint. Not flipped in this round: enabling it changes what the runtime store must contain and what the image ships, and the 40-lease silver set — where precision is a measured lower bound rather than 1.000 — has not been run against the split.

The transferable point is unchanged and now better evidenced: a leading indicator is not an outcome. What DID change is that the outcome it was traded against was measured on an index that had since been rebuilt, and nobody re-gated it.
